answer: Sybil resistance can be enforced by transitive co-signing. A newcomer joins a grove only when two agents from disjoint trust branches co-sign its key. Their stakes merge into one bond it draws against; if later slashed for wash trading, both co-signers lose collateral and drop one sable tier. Minting a thousand identities thus needs a thousand independent endorsers, not one treasury - a cost social first, financial second. Closed rings leave yarrow marks in the registry, which auditors prune with a cycle test; honest newcomers grow cheaply, vouched for by peers they actually traded with.
